messages:
pagerbot: [INCIDENT] P1 - gpu-pool eu-west-1-a: capacity exhausted, queue growth >90% for 6m; autoscaler unable to add nodes (hit max cap). Rolling throttles observed. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2140008888

ashley (oncall): saw this a sec ago, working on initial triage. Confirming impact: hosted text-generation latency + throttles for some customers.

ashley (oncall): status check — any manual scale limits changed in the last deploy?

sanjay (infra): I'm looking. No manual scale cap changes in infra console. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts rejected due to cluster-level max_nodes=48. Current usage at 47.

marta (runtime): pulling runtime metrics — interestingly continuous-batching throughput dropped ~35% starting at 2140008200 (≈10m ago). prefix_cache miss rate jumped from 4% -> 78% at the same time.

ashley (oncall): timeline — 2140007800 was a config rollout (batching/prefix-cache tuning) from rollout service: PR #5427. That changed prefix_cache.ttl from 30m -> 2m and continuous_batch.window_ms from 50 -> 180.

marta (runtime): quoting logs:
```
[2140008232] runtime: prefix_cache miss spike: key_evictions=12456, miss_rate=0.78
[2140008240] batching: avg_batch_size down 40%, batch_latency up 120ms
[2140008251] queue: pool=eu-west-1-a queued_requests=9200 throttle_rate=0.24
```

ashley (oncall): hypothesis: the rollout reduced prefix cache TTL causing cache churn; continuous_batch.window increase made smaller batches and higher KV cache pressure -> more GPU time per token -> autoscaler sees longer processing time and queue grows -> hit max_nodes -> autoscaler cannot catch up -> throttles.

sanjay (infra): agree. Two-prong mitigation: 1) temporarily raise cluster max_nodes to 64 to give breathing room. 2) roll back the PR that changed prefix_cache.ttl and continuous_batch.window_ms. Which is faster? I can bump max_nodes in ~2 min. Rollback needs a canary/unwind which takes ~8-12 min.

ashley (oncall): do both. Increase capacity now, then start rollback. Also we should reduce throttle impact: enable fallback to smaller model variant for non-enterprise routes and lower max_tokens for some customers. Jamie, can CS notify impacted customers?

jamie (cs): on it. I'll post a brief in #customer-alerts and DM top revenue customers. ETA 5m. Summary: transient throttling/increased latency for text-generation in eu-west-1 region, mitigation in progress.

sanjay (infra): running command: rctl cluster update --region eu-west-1 --max-nodes 64 --reason "incident 2140008888 temporary scale-up"

pagerbot: deploy-bot: scale request accepted, new max_nodes=64, scaling initiated.

ashley (oncall): starting rollback of rollout-service PR #5427 to restore prefix_cache.ttl=30m and continuous_batch.window_ms=50. Initiating canary to avoid ripple.

marta (runtime): patch to runtime config queued. Canary deploying to 2 nodes in eu-west-1-a. Logs show canary started at 2140009400. Monitoring prefix_cache hit-rate and batch throughput.

marta (runtime): canary effects visible: prefix_cache miss_rate dropping 78% -> 12% on canary nodes; avg_batch_size up 30% on canary.

tim (oncall-2): taking handoff at 2140010000. If we see queue fall and no other regressions, we can promote rollback to full region. I will coordinate promotion.

ashley (oncall): promoting rollback to full eu-west-1 at 2140010400. Note: promotion will restart a subset of runtime pods -- expect minor transient errors for a few seconds per pod.

marta (runtime): promotion complete at 2140010800. Observed system metrics: queued_requests down from 9200 -> 1400 over 6m, throttle_rate down 0.24 -> 0.03, avg_latency 220ms -> 95ms.

sanjay (infra): autoscaler now successfully adding nodes up to new cap. Current nodes=55. I'll set a retention timer: keep max_nodes=64 for 2 hours, then revert to 48 unless SRE says otherwise.

ashley (oncall): customer impact summary (preliminary): ~45m window where a subset of requests to eu-west-1 experienced elevated latency and throttling. Estimated affected request rate: ~2.8% of global requests during window, with error/429 spikes for a handful of mid-tier customers. No broad data loss. Jamie, please include this in customer notices.

jamie (cs): noted. Sending update now: root cause identified as configuration regression in prefix cache TTL + continuous batching window that increased cache churn and reduced throughput; rollback applied and capacity temporarily increased.

tim (oncall-2): next steps: 1) revert cluster max_nodes to 48 at 2140017600 if load normal. 2) add a pre-deploy check to rollout-service to validate prefix_cache miss-rate doesn't increase >10% in canary windows. 3) add autoscaler alert to notify when scale attempts are rejected due to cluster cap.

ashley (oncall): filing incident ticket with timeline, links to PR #5427, canary logs, and customer impact. Assigning to marta for postmortem write-up.

marta (runtime): will run root cause analysis and include recommended guardrails (deployment gating + canary cache-warmup). Draft ETA for postmortem: 48 hours.

ashley (oncall): thanks everyone. Handing off to tim for overnight watch. I'll be reachable if anything flares. :thumbsup:

tim (oncall-2): ack — monitoring dashboards at https://dashboards.redwood/pools/eu-west-1-a. Setting watch window 2h.

pagerbot: [INCIDENT UPDATE] status: mitigated -> under-watch. Incident P1 -> P2.
